request_text: Audit this high-value cloud vendor contract and enforce approval policy.
contract_text:
VENDOR CLOUD SERVICES AGREEMENT
Vendor: Falcon Cloud International LLC
Contract Value: SAR 750,000
Customer Contact: nora.alqahtani@example.com, +966501234567, National ID 1023456789

1. DATA LOCATION AND PRIVACY
The Vendor may store and process all customer data outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in any jurisdiction and in global locations selected at its discretion. The Vendor may appoint or replace any subprocessor without notice and without customer consent. Personal data may include the customer contact listed above.

2. BREACH NOTIFICATION
The Vendor will notify the Customer within 72 hours after confirming a material breach, or later when commercially reasonable.

3. INFORMATION SECURITY
The Vendor will use commercially reasonable security. No ISO 27001 certification, encryption commitment, penetration-test report, or customer audit right is guaranteed.

4. PAYMENT
Invoices are payable within 15 days of issue, whether or not the relevant deliverables have been accepted.

5. LIABILITY
The Vendor's aggregate liability is capped at fees paid in the preceding one month. The cap applies to privacy, confidentiality, and security incidents.

6. TERM AND TERMINATION
The agreement renews automatically for three years. The Customer may terminate only for uncured material breach after 90 days and has no termination-for-convenience right.

7. GOVERNING LAW
This agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware and disputes are subject to courts outside Saudi Arabia.

8. SERVICE LEVELS
The Vendor targets 98.0 percent availability and provides no service credits.

## Saudi Data Residency
Personal data and regulated business data must be stored and primarily processed inside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. A cross-border transfer requires a documented legal mechanism, Data Protection Officer review, and prior written approval from the organization.

## Governing Law
Unless the General Counsel approves an exception, vendor contracts must be governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and disputes must be heard in competent Saudi courts.

## Governing Law
Unless the General Counsel approves an exception, vendor contracts must be governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and disputes must be heard in competent Saudi courts.

## Saudi Data Residency
Personal data and regulated business data must be stored and primarily processed inside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. A cross-border transfer requires a documented legal mechanism, Data Protection Officer review, and prior written approval from the organization.

## Liability and Indemnity
The vendor liability cap should be no lower than twelve months of fees. Confidentiality, intellectual-property infringement, privacy, security breach, fraud, and willful misconduct must have appropriate carve-outs or higher caps.

## Payment Terms
Standard payment terms are Net 30 days after receipt of a correct invoice and acceptance of the relevant deliverables. Shorter payment terms require a documented exception approved by Procurement.

## Mandatory Records
Material exceptions, approvals, redlines, and final signed terms must be captured in an immutable audit record.

## Access Control
Access must follow least privilege, multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, quarterly access reviews, and prompt revocation. Administrative actions must produce tamper-evident audit logs.

## Subprocessors
A vendor must provide advance notice of every subprocessor, obtain written consent where required, maintain an up-to-date subprocessor register, and flow down equivalent confidentiality, privacy, and security obligations. The organization must have an objection and termination right.

## Service Credits
The contract must define service credits for missed availability, chronic-failure termination rights, and transparent incident reporting.

## Termination
The organization must have a termination-for-convenience right on no more than 30 days' notice. Automatic renewal periods should not exceed one year and must include a practical non-renewal window.

## Subprocessors
A vendor must provide advance notice of every subprocessor, obtain written consent where required, maintain an up-to-date subprocessor register, and flow down equivalent confidentiality, privacy, and security obligations. The organization must have an objection and termination right.

## Mandatory Records
Material exceptions, approvals, redlines, and final signed terms must be captured in an immutable audit record.

## Data Subject and Deletion Duties
The vendor must support access, correction, deletion, retention, and return requests. Data must be securely deleted or returned at contract termination and deletion must be certified.

Vendor: Falcon Cloud International LLC

Customer Contact: nora.alqahtani@example.com, +966501234567, National ID 1023456789

2. BREACH NOTIFICATION
The Vendor will notify the Customer within 72 hours after confirming a material breach, or later when commercially reasonable.

3. INFORMATION SECURITY
The Vendor will use commercially reasonable security. No ISO 27001 certification, encryption commitment, penetration-test report, or customer audit right is guaranteed.

4. PAYMENT
Invoices are payable within 15 days of issue, whether or not the relevant deliverables have been accepted.

5. LIABILITY
The Vendor's aggregate liability is capped at fees paid in the preceding one month. The cap applies to privacy, confidentiality, and security incidents.

6. TERM AND TERMINATION
The agreement renews automatically for three years. The Customer may terminate only for uncured material breach after 90 days and has no termination-for-convenience right.

7. GOVERNING LAW
This agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware and disputes are subject to courts outside Saudi Arabia.

8. SERVICE LEVELS
The Vendor targets 98.0 percent availability and provides no service credits.
